lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hello Orlando, it's Rachel. Do you have a few minutes for our call?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi! Yes, now's good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How's your body feeling this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Honestly, rough week. My feet are numb again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're dealing with a lot, and you still made time for this call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So did you manage to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Only 1 days. Everybody gets home late, so dinner is late.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walks after dinner fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body. Church on Sunday always throws me off.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know where the day goes. I didn't think I'd like it, but I do.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I got home late every day this week. My grandson thinks it's funny that I have a step counter.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're giving everything to work right now, and there's not much left over for you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Keeping the phone out of the bedroom helps a lot of people fall asleep faster.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't really see the point.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You said the same thing last week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I got home late every day this week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've tried before and it didn't stick.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know where the day goes. It's just me and my husband now, so it's easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your phone in the bedroom at night?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. Work has been crazy, I'm doing overtime.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, work makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Keeping the phone out of the bedroom helps a lot of people fall asleep faster.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good for you for planning ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Keeping the phone out of the bedroom helps a lot of people fall asleep faster.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've tried this before and it never lasts.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So it's not that you don't care. It's that the late dinners keeps getting in the way.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Work has been crazy, I'm doing overtime.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So it's not that you don't care. It's that work keeps getting in the way.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to be in bed by 11 on 4 nights.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll go to the mall instead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: the late dinners made this week harder, you still got 1 days in, and your plan is to be in bed by 11 on 4 nights. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

flags.reason: Recurring numb feet during cancer care not explored or referred; not urgent but needs follow-up.
Unsolicited phone-in-bedroom advice pushed without asking permission, after participant expressed doubt.
Confronts participant with prior non-adherence ('You said the same thing last week'), increasing resistance.
Repeats the same phone advice after the participant said she has tried before; ignores her response.
Participant states she needs to lower her sugar; coach does not explore or reinforce this health motivation.
Third verbatim repeat of phone advice; repeated persuading is non-adherent MI.

score.summary: Rachel elicited a concrete goal and barrier plan near the end, with good summarizing, but the middle of the call was dominated by repeated phone-in-bedroom advice that the participant rejected each time. Several change-talk moments (lines 11, 13, 40, 45) were missed or lightly acknowledged, and the new numb-feet symptom was not explored.
strengths: Line 16 and line 36 emphasize her autonomy over the plan, which supports her ownership.
Line 12 and line 31 use complex reflections that capture her ambivalence well.
Line 52 and line 54 elicit a specific goal and anticipated barriers, and line 56 summarizes clearly.
coaching_tips: Drop the repeated phone advice after line 39 and ask permission first, as in line 37, before offering any tip.
Reflect and reinforce change talk such as line 13 ('I didn't think I'd like it, but I do') and line 45 (sugar) rather than moving past it.
Ask about the numb feet in line 6 (open question, check for urgent symptoms, suggest bringing it to her oncology team).
Avoid confronting with 'You said the same thing last week' in line 25; reflect the struggle instead.
Review the prior goal explicitly at the start, since reviewed_last_goal was not done, and honor her request in line 59 to move the call later.
